- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.5) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.5) and prices are rising, model often underestimates the spike; increase forecast by 1–3% to capture momentum.  
- Model consistently underestimates late-period (last 5–7 days) price increases, especially after sentiment turns positive; apply a 1–2% upward bias to final 5–7 days.  
- Model frequently overshoots early in the forecast horizon (first 3–5 days) after a spike; cap forecast at 10–15% below true peak for first 3 days.  
- If sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., from -1.5 to +1.0 within 3 days), model often fails to adjust; apply a 2–5% downward correction to forecast 3–5 days ahead.  
- Mean reversion is evident in 30-day forecasts: if model is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–3% for next 5 days; if below, increase by 1–2%.  
- Sentiment volatility >0.5 in 3 consecutive days triggers a 1–2% upward adjustment to forecast to account for uncertainty.
